# Requirements Document: Seller follow-up actions on an airline change

## Introduction

When the airline changes an order, it sends the seller a change notice.  The
notice may ask the seller to act: accept the change, reshop, cancel, contact
the airline, or reprice and accept.  Each follow-up action may carry a time
limit and a consequence that applies if the seller has not acted by then.  A
notice with no follow-up action needs only acknowledgement.  The sources leave
two things open, so the model takes them as a parameter, a reading of the
sources: what applies when a time limit passes and no consequence is stated,
and whether contacting the airline, which happens outside the order, is
recorded as the seller's answer.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/FollowUp.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/FollowUp.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-701

**User Story:** As a seller, I want each change notice to show whether it waits for me, what I answered, or what the airline did when I did not answer, so that I can tell the customer where their trip stands.

**Rule:** WHEN an airline change notice offers follow-up actions THE SYSTEM SHALL keep them pending until the seller answers with one of them or a consequence of inaction applies. (Lean: `resolve`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an airline change notice carries no follow-up action THE SYSTEM SHALL ask the seller only to acknowledge it.
   - ONE-701.1, proven: proven theorem `resolve_acknowledge_only`; example `noticeStandings`
2. WHEN the seller performs an offered Accept, Reshop, Cancel or RepriceAndAccept action before any consequence of inaction applies THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve the notice with the seller's answer.
   - ONE-701.2, proven: proven theorem `resolve_answers`; example `noticeStandings`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve a notice with an answer only when the seller took that action, the notice offers it, and the seller took it before any consequence of inaction applied.
   - ONE-701.3, proven: proven theorem `resolve_answered_sound`
4. WHILE the seller has not answered a notice that offers follow-up actions THE SYSTEM SHALL keep it pending until a consequence of inaction applies, and then resolve it with that consequence.
   - ONE-701.4, proven: proven theorem `resolve_unanswered`; example `noticeStandings`
5. WHEN the seller contacts the airline about a notice that offers ContactAirline before any consequence of inaction applies THE SYSTEM SHALL apply no consequence of inaction.
   - ONE-701.5, open: open theorem `contact_airline_answers`; counterexample `contactThenAutoAccept`

#### Open question on ONE-701.5

> When the seller contacts the airline about a notice that offers
> ContactAirline, before any consequence of inaction applies, no consequence of
> inaction is applied.
>
> Open question for the business.  Contacting the airline happens outside the
> order, and the sources do not say whether the order records it or whether it
> clears the other pending actions.  Under a reading where it is not recorded,
> a seller who phones the airline before the time limit still sees
> Auto-acceptance applied when the limit passes.  The example
> `contactThenAutoAccept` shows it.  Does contacting the airline count as
> an answer, and does it stop the time limit?

### Requirement ONE-702

**User Story:** As a seller, I want to know what happens if I do not answer a change notice in time, so that the customer is not surprised by an outcome nobody chose.

**Rule:** WHEN a time limit of a change notice passes and the seller has not answered THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the consequence of inaction of the follow-up action whose time limit passed first. (Lean: `consequenceAt`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a time limit that carries a consequence of inaction passes THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the consequence of a follow-up action whose time limit is the earliest.
   - ONE-702.1, proven: proven theorem `lapse_applies_earliest`; example `autoCancellation`; example `noticeStandings`
2. IF no follow-up action of a notice has a time limit THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL apply no consequence of inaction.
   - ONE-702.2, proven: proven theorem `no_limit_no_consequence`; example `noticesAtDeparture`
3. WHILE no time limit of a notice has passed THE SYSTEM SHALL apply no consequence of inaction.
   - ONE-702.3, proven: proven theorem `before_limits_no_consequence`; example `noticeStandings`
4. IF the seller does not answer a change notice that carries follow-up actions THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve it before the affected flight departs.
   - ONE-702.4, open: open theorem `resolved_before_departure`; counterexample `noticesAtDeparture`

#### Open question on ONE-702.4

> A notice that offers follow-up actions is resolved before the affected
> flight departs, even if the seller never answers.
>
> Open question for the business.  The sources make both the time limit and the
> consequence optional, and do not tie the time limit to the departure.  A
> notice that offers Cancel with neither, like the guide's Cancel example, never
> lapses; a time limit set after the departure lapses too late.  The example
> `noticesAtDeparture` shows both still unresolved when the flight departs.
> What applies when a follow-up action has no time limit or no consequence, and
> must the time limit fall before the affected flight departs?
